--- title: "Build a simple chatbot for your small‑business site with Cohere" subtitle: "A step-by-step guide to setting up an AI chatbot on your website using Cohere — if the visual builder is available, no coding is needed!" category: "guide" audience: "business" company: "Cohere" tool: "Cohere" level: "beginner" read_time_minutes: 6 tags: ["getting-started", "cohere", "chatbot"] --- # Build a simple chatbot for your small‑business site with Cohere By the end of this guide, you’ll have a live chatbot on your website ready to answer your most common customer questions. The steps assume you’re using Cohere’s visual builder **if it is available**; otherwise you can achieve the same result by using Cohere’s API and a small amount of custom code. ## Before you start - **Cohere Account:** A free or paid Cohere account. The steps in this guide work with a free plan, though paid plans offer higher usage limits. - **Website Access:** Ability to add custom HTML/JavaScript to your site (e.g., via WordPress, Wix, Squarespace, Shopify, etc.). - **Common Questions:** A list of the top 3‑5 questions your customers frequently ask. - **Time:** Allocate about 20‑30 minutes. ## Step 1 — Create your Cohere account Visit `cohere.com` and click the **Sign up** (or **Register**) button. Follow the prompts, verify your email, and you’ll be taken to the Cohere dashboard. *You’ll know it worked when you see the Cohere console or dashboard after logging in.* ## Step 2 — Start a new chatbot project (if applicable) If Cohere’s current interface includes a **Projects** or **Dashboard** area, look for a **New Project** or **Create Chatbot** button and give your bot a name (e.g., `ShopHelper`). *If the visual project UI is no longer present, you can instead create a chatbot by using the Cohere Chat API – see Cohere’s API documentation for creating a bot endpoint.* ## Step 3 — Build conversations (if a visual editor exists) If Cohere still offers a visual editor, you can add **Question** and **Answer** blocks, linking them to form simple conversation flows. *If the visual editor has been removed, define your conversation logic by writing prompt‑response pairs in your code and sending them to the Cohere Chat API.* ## Step 4 — Generate or obtain embed code (conditional) If Cohere provides an **Embed** or **Deploy** option, you can generate a widget snippet that looks similar to the example below. Copy the generated code. ```html
``` *If no embed widget is offered, you’ll need to integrate the chatbot manually. Use the Cohere Chat API from your website’s JavaScript (or server‑side) to send user messages and display responses in a custom UI.* ## Step 5 — Add the widget or custom integration to your website - **If you have a widget snippet:** Paste the code into your site’s HTML just before the closing `` tag (or use the CMS’s custom‑code feature). - **If you are using the API:** Insert your custom JavaScript that calls the Cohere Chat endpoint and renders the chat UI where you want it to appear. After publishing, visit your live site and look for a chat bubble (or your custom UI) in the bottom‑right corner. ## Common mistakes - Forgetting to publish the HTML changes. - Leaving response placeholders blank, which can cause generic fallback replies. - Placing the snippet in a part of the page that isn’t rendered (e.g., inside a `` tag). - If using the API, forgetting to include your API key securely. ## What this means for you - **For everyday life:** You can automate answers to routine queries, saving time. - **For your business:** The assistant works 24/7, handling common questions so you can focus on higher‑value tasks. - **If you’re just starting:** Begin with a single question‑answer pair, then expand. ## Try it now Open your Cohere dashboard (or API console), create a new chatbot (or set up an API endpoint), and add a simple question‑answer pair such as “What is your return policy?” → “Returns are accepted within 30 days with a receipt.” If you have a widget, embed the generated code; otherwise, add a small JavaScript snippet that calls the Cohere Chat API.
